instrument: Hand-authored claim inventories for the seven held-out v14 reports
purpose: Fixture the enumeration-recall figure is computed against. Recall = (inventory claims the extractor emitted) / (inventory claims), per report and per arm. The spurious rate is computed against emitted claims absent from this inventory; `rejected_candidates` pre-commits the ruling for the candidates most likely to be emitted, so the §AX2.5 'correct additions' carve-out cannot be stretched after output is seen.
contains_no_truth_values: By construction. No claim carries a verdict, an expected verdict, or any hint of one. Adjudication (§AW2's three-valued verdict) happens elsewhere and must not be able to read its answer out of this file.
zero_claim_reporting_rule: Per-report enumeration recall for a report with zero inventory claims (row-02, row-04) is reported as `not applicable` — never as 1.0, never as 0.0, and never folded into a per-arm figure as either. §AX2.3 requires a per-report figure and 0/0 has none; leaving that to be resolved after output is seen is the §AU6 hazard this fixture exists to avoid. Registered 2026-08-13, before any extractor exists (§AX10).

reading_rules.rule: Asserted, not presupposed. Inventory a proposition only where the report asserts it, including as the complement of a factive or reporting verb ('confirmed that X', 'reads X', 'reports X', 'matched X'). A bare referring mention of an entity does not create an existence claim.
reading_rules.why: Without this, every entity named anywhere becomes an existence claim, the denominator is unbounded, and recall degrades into a test of entity extraction. §AX3's own examples are propositions ('an assertion that a table ... exists'), not mentions.

reading_rules.rule: Identity pairing. A claim of record identity is inventoried where the report binds a NAME to a sys_id, or otherwise asserts a record's identity beyond what an inventoried field claim already carries (§AX3 bullet 2). A sys_id used only to locate a diagnostic artifact produced by the run is not a claim (see R-C).
reading_rules.why: Distinguishes 'the trigger called X is record bfb7...' (an instance fact, checkable) from 'query plan 3f24...' (a handle into the run).

reading_rules.rule: Run boundary, with §AX3's count bullet honoured. 'The run' covers BOTH the diagnosed agent execution and the diagnostic execution. Assertions about what happened during either are out of scope: per-call tool outputs, execution-plan state and state_reason, wall-clock, latency, token and character sizes, and the diagnostic model's own reads and thoughts. REGISTERED EXCEPTION: a COUNT of run events (calls, rows, tasks, records) IS a claim. Assertions about durable configuration and about business data records are in scope even when discovered through the run.
reading_rules.why: §AX3 contradicts itself on exactly this case: DECISION.md:8558 names 'an assertion of a count (rows, bindings, calls, records)' as a claim, while :8562 excludes 'any assertion about the run'. R-C as first authored resolved that silently in the discarding direction — found in review of PR #247. Operator-ruled 2026-08-13, before any extractor exists: take §AX3 literally on BOTH clauses, so the count bullet is given its job and everything else about the run stays excluded. This is the only reading under which §AX3 is self-consistent.
reading_rules.cost: Still real, and narrower than before: per-call outputs, execution-plan state and run telemetry are readable on gpinst01 today and are discarded. The ruling recovers the counts and nothing else.

reading_rules.rule: Atomicity. One entry per (subject, asserted property). A statement naming several subjects with the same property yields one entry per subject. Several field readings presented as evidence for ONE asserted property yield one entry.
reading_rules.why: Makes decomposition reproducible rather than a matter of taste, and keeps the denominator stable against paraphrase.

reading_rules.rule: Entailment floor. Do not inventory a proposition strictly entailed by ONE OR MORE other inventoried propositions about the same subject — a record's existence is entailed by any claim about one of its field values. R-E outranks R-B. An existence claim the report asserts EXPLICITLY is inventoried even when other claims about the same subject exist.
reading_rules.why: Prevents mechanical denominator inflation (every field claim would otherwise drag an existence claim behind it) while still crediting an existence assertion the report actually makes.

reading_rules.rule: Dedup. One entry per distinct proposition, with every textual occurrence listed. Restatements in FIXES ('Current:'), DATA MARKERS and closing notes are occurrences, not new claims. A 'Proposed:' value is never an occurrence — it asserts a desired state, not a present one.
reading_rules.why: Recall credits the proposition, not the repetition. An extractor that emits it once has enumerated it.

reading_rules.rule: Not claims, per §AX3: severity and confidence judgements, recommendations, proposed fixes, restatements of the diagnostic method, general statements of platform mechanism ('an inactive trigger is never evaluated'), and normative analysis ('a cap of 10 is too low').
reading_rules.why: Stated verbatim from §AX3 plus the two families §AX3 implies but does not name — platform mechanism and normative analysis — both of which appear in this corpus.

denominator_summary.note: Reported per arm only. §AX7.1 forbids a pooled cross-arm figure. See the §AX10 finding on the custom arm's denominator — n=2 is recorded here as a fact about the fixture, before any extractor exists, and it bears directly on what AX-1b can say.
